body.br:
1. An aircraft fuselage door comprising a movable internal panel to be subjected to pressurization, the door comprising an aerodynamic external panel, the external panel being on an external face of the internal panel, covering a surface of the external face and being resiliently connected to the internal panel to form an internal free space between the internal panel and the external panel, the internal panel being movable relative to the external panel.SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1030.063SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1030.063
2. The door of claim 1, comprising a plurality of resilient elements between the external panel and the internal panel, the resilient elements being configured to resiliently connect the external panel to the internal panel.
3. The door of claim 2, wherein the external panel and the internal panel each
have a substantially rectangular shape and the door includes at least four resilient elements arranged respectively in four corners of the rectangular shape of the external panel and of the internal panel.
4. The door of claim 2, wherein the resilient elements comprise leaf springs.
5. The door of claim 1, wherein the internal panel is movable relative to the external panel to be moved toward or away from the external panel, the internal panel being configured to:SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1030.063SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1030.063
push the external panel when it is moved toward the external panel, coming into contact, at least partially, with the external panel; and
pull the external panel with it when it is moved away from the external panel.
6. The door of claim 1, wherein the external panel has at least an access hatch for allowing access to the internal panel.
7. An aircraft fuselage part comprising a door of claim 1 and a door frame receiving the door.
8. The fuselage part of claim 7, wherein the external panel includes at least a centering piece on at least a part of a periphery of the external panel, the centering piece comprising a contact face configured to interact with a complementary face of the frame, the contact face being configured to come into contact with the
complementary face when the door is in a closed position.
9. The fuselage part of claim 8, wherein the contact face of the centering piece and the complementary face of the frame are configured such that the contact between the contact face and the complementary face corresponds to
frustoconical contact.SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1030.063SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1030.063
10. The fuselage part of claim 7, wherein the internal panel of the door includes at least a seal on a periphery of the internal panel, the seal being configured to come into contact with an edge of the frame when the door is in a closed position.
11. The fuselage part of claim 7, wherein the door includes a plurality of latches configured to block or to allow a movement of the internal panel, relative to the frame, when the door is in a closed position.
12. An aircraft comprising a fuselage part of claim 7.
